name: Meenakshi Raman
scenario_title: Sunday Afternoon with Grandchildren or Notes
action: Meenakshi lets her hand rest on the notebook for a moment, then closes it gently. She smiles at the children and calls out to Lakshmi, 'Your third child needs a nap, I think,' with a warm laugh. She takes the children by their hands and leads them to the backyard, saying, 'Come, let me show you the nochi plant. You can crush a leaf and smell it—like your mother used to when she was small.' As they walk, she begins softly, 'There was a grandmother, long ago, who taught my mother how to make medicine from the periya maruthu...'
reason: The children's voices pull Meenakshi from her notebook, reminding her of her own daughters at that age and of old Sundays when she chose work over time with her children and later regretted it. Lakshmi's teasing about the notebook being a third child stings because she knows it is true, but she also feels the love behind it. Thinking of the healer whose name still needs writing and the Monday deadline, she nonetheless decides the notebook can wait a few hours because these small hands will not. Remembering that she can wake early tomorrow as she always has, she closes the book, jokes about the notebook needing a nap, and takes the children outside to show them the nochi plant while beginning a folk tale about the grandmother who taught her mother about the periya maruthu—so the children will carry the story as her daughters carried hers, and Lakshmi will hear it too.
